objective: Define the smallest native Verilator option-parser boundary that can hand off to the existing sidecar plan contract without claiming a native parser implementation yet.

parser_boundary.operator_goal: A normal Verilator build invocation should be able to add a compact sidecar GPU acceleration option and produce the same inspectable sidecar handoff contract now exposed by the wrapper and shim.
parser_owned_responsibilities: parse --sim-accel and accept only sidecar-gpu in the first native boundary
require --sim-accel-states and --sim-accel-steps as a positive-integer pair
reject missing shape halves, non-positive counts, unknown accelerators, and mixed native shape spellings
preserve ordinary Verilator inputs such as --cc, --timing, -Mdir, source files, -f filelists, --top-module, defines, warning flags, and other Verilator arguments
emit or call a structured sidecar-plan handoff instead of relying on scraped command strings
keep the parse/plan result inspectable before any execution
sidecar_owned_responsibilities_kept_out_: not-ready stage inspection for resident modes and dataset-backed flows
terminal print modes and JSON operator-plan convenience output
required_handoff_fields: source files or explicit filelist inputs
coverage overlay or coverage top boundary
coverage manifest scope and compared output words
compare report path or deterministic naming rule

required_next_gate.name: review_verilator_native_option_parser_boundary_gate
must_decide: whether the definition keeps the boundary parser-only and no-execution
whether the expanded future-Verilator spelling is the native minimum while --sim-accel-shape remains wrapper compatibility
whether the parser-owned responsibilities are separate from wrapper/shim print modes, target registry lookup, and sidecar execution
whether the handoff field list is sufficient for mdir, top module, source boundary, state files, compare report path, and coverage_output_equivalence
whether invalid accelerator names, missing states/steps halves, non-positive counts, and mixed shape spellings are correctly assigned to the compatibility mapper for later dry-run checks
whether resident modes and dataset-backed targets remain outside the direct native-parser handoff
whether the next reviewed action may be a non-executing dry-run gate
whether the result avoids native Verilator parser support, arbitrary RTL support, dependency inference, automatic optimal GPU allocation, and new timing claims

non_claims: not a native Verilator parser implementation
not automatic optimal GPU allocation for any design
not a runtime or ABI change
not a new public CLI or workflow
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
